notes:
1. Meaning of National Symbols

  • National symbols represent the identity, sovereignty, heritage and unity of India.

They connect citizens with:

  • National history.
  • Constitutional values.
  • Cultural heritage.
  • Freedom struggle.

2. Major National Symbols

Important symbols for TNPSC include:

  • National Flag.
  • State Emblem of India.
  • National Anthem.
  • National Song.
  • National Calendar.
  • National Animal.
  • National Bird.
  • National Flower.
  • National Tree.
  • National Fruit.
  • National Aquatic Animal.
  • National River.

3. National Flag

  • The National Flag of India is popularly known as the Tiranga or Tricolour.
📌 Must-Memorise

National Flag → Tiranga

4. Adoption of National Flag

  • The Constituent Assembly adopted the present National Flag on 22 July 1947.
📌 Must-Memorise

National Flag Adopted → 22 July 1947

5. Before Independence

  • The flag was adopted shortly before India became independent on 15 August 1947.

6. Shape of National Flag

  • The National Flag is rectangular.

7. Flag Ratio

  • The ratio of the width to the length of the National Flag is 2:3.
📌 Must-Memorise

Flag Ratio → 2:3

8. Three Colours

The flag consists of three equal horizontal bands:

  • India saffron at the top.
  • White in the middle.
  • India green at the bottom.

9. Ashoka Chakra

  • A navy-blue Ashoka Chakra appears in the centre of the white band.
📌 Must-Memorise

Ashoka Chakra → Navy Blue

10. Number of Spokes

  • The Ashoka Chakra has 24 spokes.
📌 Must-Memorise

Ashoka Chakra → 24 Spokes

11. Source of Ashoka Chakra

  • The Chakra is based on the Dharma Chakra associated with the Lion Capital of Ashoka at Sarnath.

12. Earlier Flag Symbol

  • Earlier Congress versions of the flag contained a spinning wheel or charkha.
  • The final National Flag adopted in 1947 replaced the charkha with the Ashoka Chakra.
⚠️ TNPSC Trap

Earlier Nationalist Flag → Charkha
National Flag of India → Ashoka Chakra

  • Pingali Venkayya presented flag designs during the national movement.

It consisted of:

  • White.

  • The 1931 flag became an important predecessor of the present National Flag.

20. White

Article 51A(a) of the Constitution requires every citizen to respect:

  • The Constitution.
  • Its ideals and institutions.
  • The National Flag.
  • The National Anthem.
📌 Must-Memorise

Article 51A(a) → National Flag + National Anthem

  • The full version of the National Anthem takes approximately 52 seconds.

  • Bijoe Emmanuel v. State of Kerala (1986) involved schoolchildren who respectfully stood during the National Anthem but did not sing because of their religious beliefs.

  • The Supreme Court protected their freedom of conscience because they did not show disrespect to the National Anthem.
🔗 TNPSC Key Link

Bijoe Emmanuel → National Anthem + Freedom of Conscience

  • Vaishakha.
  • Jyaishtha.
  • Ashadha.
  • Shravana.
  • Bhadra.
  • Ashvina.

  • Agrahayana.

  • The next five months after Chaitra have 31 days each.

  • The remaining six months have 30 days each.
